newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition ally in key government meetings.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition ally in key government meetings.

text.p: Tansu Ciller's secularist True Path Party will debate pulling out of its shaky coalition with Turkey's ruling Islamists at a series of meetings in the coming days, party officials said on Wednesday.
Ciller, also the foreign minister, will listen to her MPs' opinions on the government's future at a closed-door session in parliament on Wednesday morning.
"The general administrative council will then meet, probably tomorrow, and evaluate the trend," a party official told Reuters.
The government has slowly been crumbling since the army began pushing it to crack down on Islamist activism in February.
The press said Ciller would ask the party for the authority to demand that Prime Minister Nemcettin Erbakan hand over power to her to take the country to early elections.

Ciller may pull out of the coalition if Erbakan disagrees, the Sabah daily said. "If he does not stand down he is acting contrary to the coalition protocol and we will have to withdraw," it quoted an unnamed True Path minister as saying.
Other papers said Erbakan and Ciller disagreed at a meeting on Tuesday on how and when to hold early polls to clear up the political crisis. Elections are due by the year 2000.
